summary: Thin day for evidence: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked or unsearchable here, so every source below is a Hacker News thread from the last 5 days. The strongest theme is people refusing subscription-locked or bloated vendor software for hardware they already own (an embroidery-machine Show HN drew 357 points and a pile of Cricut/Hatch complaints). Smaller themes: GPU rental price-vs-reliability confusion, sites nagging desktop users to install the app, startups shutting down APIs with little warning, and Mac-only tools people want elsewhere.

ideas.title: Subscription-Free Companion App for Cricut and Embroidery Machines
ideas.oneLiner: A browser app (Web Bluetooth/USB export) that designs and sends jobs to cheap craft machines so owners never pay the maker's subscription.
ideas.problem: Hobby cutting and embroidery machines are sold cheap, then the bundled software is crippled behind a subscription or the good third-party tools cost over $1,000. HN readers cheered a dev who reverse-engineered a $300 Brother machine, and others immediately asked for the same for Cricut.
ideas.targetUsers: Hobbyists and small Etsy sellers who own a Cricut, Brother or similar craft machine and make patches, stickers or merch.
ideas.monetization: Free tier with basic design and export; one-time ~$29-49 Pro unlock (auto-digitizing, fonts, templates) rather than a subscription, which is the selling point.
mvp: SVG/PNG import with simple fill and outline stitch generation
Export to common embroidery formats (DST, PES) and cut formats (SVG)
Web Bluetooth send for one popular machine (Brother PP1 first)
Built-in text and shape tools with a few free fonts
Compatibility list page showing exactly which machines work

ideas.title: GPU Rental Tracker: Price Plus Real Availability and Provision Success
ideas.oneLiner: A comparison site that shows hourly GPU prices across clouds and also whether instances actually start and perform.
ideas.problem: The same H100 ranged from $2.69 to $12.29 an hour, but cheap marketplace hosts often hang, have stuck processes, slow disks or no capacity. Price tables exist, but users say price is meaningless without knowing if you can get a working box.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie ML developers, researchers and startups renting GPUs for fine-tuning, inference and training.
ideas.monetization: Free price table; paid alerts and API ($9-19/month) for price-drop and availability notifications; affiliate links to providers.
mvp: Daily price scrape from the public APIs of 8-10 GPU providers
Filter by GPU model, VRAM, on-demand versus spot and region
Crowd-sourced 'did it start / disk speed / dropped' report button per provider
Email alert when a chosen GPU drops below a target price
Cost-per-job calculator using throughput reports

ideas.title: Open-in-App Nag Remover for Desktop Browsers
ideas.oneLiner: An extension that removes 'get the app' overlays and scroll locks on Reddit, Substack and similar sites, kept current by a shared rules list.
ideas.problem: Sites now throw a full-page popup pushing the mobile app at desktop users, even on Linux, and disable scrolling. Users respond by leaving the site instead of fighting it.
ideas.targetUsers: Desktop browser users who read Reddit, Substack, Quora, Medium and similar sites.
ideas.monetization: Free core; $12/year for auto-updating rules, sync across browsers, and per-site custom picker.
mvp: Detect and remove app-install overlays and restore page scrolling
Starter rules for Reddit, Substack, Quora, Medium and Pinterest
One-click 'hide this nag' element picker that saves a rule
Community rule updates fetched daily
Chrome and Firefox builds

ideas.title: Local Meeting Notes with Speaker Labels for Windows and Linux
ideas.oneLiner: A bot-free, on-device meeting transcriber and summarizer that labels who said what and runs on Windows and Linux, not just Mac.
ideas.problem: Users are leaving subscription meeting-note tools for local alternatives, but the new open-source options lean Mac-only, and bot-free recording loses speaker names. Windows and Linux users are left out.
ideas.targetUsers: Consultants, founders and engineers on Windows or Linux who want private, subscription-free meeting notes.
ideas.monetization: One-time $39 license or free with a paid sync/team-summary add-on; avoid a recurring fee as positioning.
mvp: System-audio plus mic capture on Windows
On-device transcription with automatic model choice by hardware
Speaker names pulled from Zoom/Meet/Teams window titles with manual rename
Summary and action-item template
Export to Markdown and Notion

ideas.title: Vendor Wind-Down Radar for Developer APIs and Hosting
ideas.oneLiner: Watches the APIs and platforms you depend on for shutdown signs and tells you early, with migration alternatives.
ideas.problem: Two developer services (Val Town and an LLM API) announced shutdowns in the same week, one by a bare email with no blog post that readers first took for phishing. Developers who built on them had little warning and no ready alternative list.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie developers and small teams who depend on third-party APIs, hosting and AI model providers.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 tracked vendors; $8/month for unlimited vendors, email/Slack alerts and migration checklists.
mvp: Paste your package.json or env keys to detect vendors you use
Watch vendor blogs, status pages and changelogs for wind-down wording
Alert via email or Slack with the shutdown date
Curated alternatives list for each vendor
Verified-source check so shutdown emails can be told apart from phishing

competitors.name: AlternativeTo

ideas.title: Who Used My PC? Intruder and Kid-Use Alerts for Windows and iPhone
ideas.oneLiner: A Windows (and later phone) app that photographs whoever uses the device while you're away and sends the photo to your phone.
ideas.problem: A Mac-only app that photos unknown users drew immediate requests for versions on other platforms, including from a parent who does not want kids using the PC when out of the room but dislikes PIN prompts.
ideas.targetUsers: Windows users, parents and people sharing a home or office computer.
ideas.monetization: Free local logging; one-time $4.99-9.99 for remote alerts, matching what the Mac app charges.
mvp: Detect lock-screen activity, unlock and activity after idle
Take a webcam photo and compare with owner's face locally
Local timeline of access events
Push alert via Telegram, ntfy or email
Kid mode: alert when device is used during set hours
